In Finland, changes have been stronger than the OECD average. This is fatal for Finland's future, as Finland can only succeed through knowledge.

fi-kk-421-2026.f: Written question on the impact of data centre investments on electricity adequacy in Finland
fi-kk-421-2026.s: I asked Environment Minister Multala earlier about the impact of Google's massive investment in data centre on electricity adequacy in Finland (KK 367/2026 vp). Minister Multala replied that "Google has announced that he will support new electricity generation in Finland and other investments in the electricity system. The company has contractually supported wind power capacity in Finland for a total of 629 megawatts."
fi-kk-421-2026.t: On the impact of investment in the Data Centre on electricity adequacy in Finland

fi-kk-422-2026.f: Written question on the implementation of bear quota hunting and the reasons for the related EU legal uncertainties
fi-kk-422-2026.s: In December 2025, the Parliament of Finland adopted a declaration in connection with the amendment of the hunting law that the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry should prepare, without delay, the regulations necessary to depart from the restrain of the bear and lynch by hunting under a regional quota.
fi-kk-422-2026.t: on the implementation of quota hunting for bear and the grounds for the related EU legal uncertainties

fi-kk-423-2026.f: Written question on imports of Russian nickel rock and unwrought nickel
fi-kk-423-2026.s: The EU's Russian sanctions prohibit imports of Russian copper throughout the production chain, including copper rock (CN 7401). The EU 20 and 21 sanctions package banned imports of several Russian nickel products (CN 7503-7505) and nickel and copper ores. However, nickel (CN 7501) and unwrought nickel (CN 7502) are currently excluded from the scope of the ban.
fi-kk-423-2026.t: Imports of Russian nickel rock and unwrought nickel

fi-kk-424-2026.f: Written question on closed areas for fisheries
fi-kk-424-2026.s: In Finland, the number of projects aimed at bypassing or removing hiking barriers has increased in the 2020s. In 2024, more migration barriers were passed or removed in Finland than in any other European country (Dam Removal Europe 2024).

fi-kk-425-2026.f: Written question on the vignette charge for heavy traffic
fi-kk-425-2026.s: The poor condition of the Finnish road network and the operating conditions in the transport sector are once again at the heart of the transport policy debate. The framework funds for basic road management have been cut to a record low level for the coming years.
fi-kk-425-2026.t: On the vignette charge for heavy traffic

fi-kk-426-2026.f: Written question about the mass graves in Chemann
fi-kk-426-2026.s: In the northern part of Sri Lanka, a mass tomb of Chemann in Jaffa has been dug up by mid-August 2026, and according to the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), there are also bodies of children among the dead. Media reports that the mass grave has also found everyday items of the deceased, such as school packs and milk bottles.
fi-kk-426-2026.t: From the mass graves of Chemann

fi-kk-427-2026.f: Written question on actions against human rights and rainbow activists in Turkey
fi-kk-427-2026.s: On 12 and 13 September, Turkey witnessed a serious attack on the rainbow community and the civil society defending it. Authorities arrested rainbow activists and human rights defenders and raided the premises of 16 rainbow organisations across the country.
fi-kk-427-2026.t: on actions against human rights and rainbow activists in Turkey

fi-kk-428-2026.f: Written question on the contribution of volunteering to income security
fi-kk-428-2026.s: Volunteering is a key part of Finnish society, which strengthens inclusion and communitarianism, as well as complements public services in a wide range of ways, including social and health organisations, older people and youth work, cultural and event activities, sports and sports clubs, crisis work and business twinning.
fi-kk-428-2026.t: The impact of voluntary work on income security

fi-kk-429-2026.f: Written question on the further preparation of the Tampere-Turku train connection
fi-kk-429-2026.s: The development of the Tampere-Turku-Naantalrailway link as part of the ongoing passenger train tendering process has already been blocked before its challenges and opportunities have been openly assessed.
fi-kk-429-2026.t: Making Tampere-Turku train connection ready for further preparation

fi-kk-430-2026.f: The written question of extending the period of parental leave to seven years after the birth of the child
fi-kk-430-2026.s: The reform of family leave entered into force in August 2022. Many things changed for the better: the number of fathers' family leave increased, the use of parental leave became more flexible, the reconciliation of family life and work was facilitated, and the whole system was simplified.
fi-kk-430-2026.t: extending the period of parental benefit to seven years from the birth of the child

fi-kk-431-2026.f: Written question on links between wolf quota hunting, wild boar stock and African swine fever
fi-kk-431-2026.s: In winter 2026, a quota hunt for a wolf, defined as threatened in Finland, was carried out in the South East-Finland area, where wolves were also killed. Based on DNA analyses by the Natural Resources Centre, the South West-Finland quota area also identified dog wolves, whose removal has been considered important in maintaining the genetic purity of the wolf population.
fi-kk-431-2026.t: on the links between wolf quota hunting, wild boar stock and African swine fever

fi-kk-432-2026.f: Written question on the development of polytechnic education for clinics
fi-kk-432-2026.s: The skills and responsibilities of clinics have increased as a result of the rapid development of veterinary, therapeutic and technological processes. However, the current education system does not fully meet the changed skills needs of the industry. In Finland, the training of clinician nurses is based mainly on vocational qualifications and there is no own polytechnic degree in the field.
fi-kk-432-2026.t: Development of polytechnic education for clinics

fi-kk-433-2026.f: Written question on the status of drug cannabis and the exercise of patients' rights
fi-kk-433-2026.s: Many Finns do not get the herbal medicine they need because they require special permission, and getting a prescription is more difficult.
fi-kk-433-2026.t: The role of medical cannabis and the realisation of patients' rights

fi-kk-434-2026.f: Written question on strengthening the needs-based nature of the therapy programme
fi-kk-434-2026.s: The therapy guarantee is based on the citizens' initiative KAA 10/2019, submitted to the Parliament of Finland in 2019, which received over 50 000 statements of support. The aim of the draft law was to ensure rapid access for all to therapeutic psychotherapy or other psychosocial care after the first visit to the health centre.
fi-kk-434-2026.t: Strengthening the needs-based nature of therapy ataxia

fi-kk-436-2026.f: The written question of making the cost of voluntary tick vaccination tax deductible
fi-kk-436-2026.s: TBE is a tick-brain disease that has been transmitted by ticks and has increased number of cases in Finland in the long term. The disease can be prevented by vaccination. The so-called tick vaccine protects against tick-brain infection, but not from borreliosis or tick bites.

fi-kk-437-2026.s: section 21 of the Finnish Constitution provides everyone with the right to be properly and without undue delay, and the right to be heard, to have a reasoned decision and to appeal. section 22 of the Constitution obliges the public authorities to ensure the fulfilment of fundamental and human rights. fi-kk-438-2026.f: The written question of reducing the administrative burden on banking services of small associations
fi-kk-438-2026.s: Small village associations, leisure associations and other non-profit organisations are doing valuable work to promote local community, leisure opportunities and the well-being of people, which are largely based on voluntary work, and the annual financial flows of many associations are only a few hundred or thousands of euros.

fi-kk-440-2026.f: Written question on the placement of icebreakers in northern Finland
fi-kk-440-2026.s: The changed safety environment in Finland has highlighted the importance of security of supply, logistics capacity and critical infrastructure for national security. A significant part of Finnish industrial exports pass through the ports of northern Finland, which makes the ports of the Bothnian Sea region essential, especially for the forestry, steel, mining and energy sectors, both in everyday life and in the exceptional situation.
fi-kk-440-2026.t: from the installation of icebreakers in northern Finland

fi-kk-441-2026.f: The written question of rising energy prices and safeguarding public transport conditions
fi-kk-441-2026.s: Higher energy prices have recently increased cost pressures for households, agriculture and industry. The uncertainty of the international environment and the impact of the situation in the Middle East on the energy markets underline the need to assess ways to mitigate the effects of energy price volatility in Finland.
fi-kk-441-2026.t: Energy price increases and public transport conditions

fi-la-30-2026.f: Act amending section 24 of the Welfare Act
fi-la-30-2026.s: The aim of the initiative is to reduce the number of persons authorised in welfare areas by their own decision below the current minimum. The number of persons authorised in welfare areas is laid down in Article 24 of the Welfare Code. The minimum number of persons authorised in the territory of 200 000 inhabitants is 59, in the area of 200 001 to 400 000, 69 delegates in the region of 400 001 to 600 000.
fi-la-30-2026.t: Amendment of section 24 of the Welfare Act

fi-la-36-2026.f: Legislative initiative amending section 53 of the Health Act, sections 25a and 45 of the Social Welfare Act and section 10a of the Law on Higher Education.
fi-la-36-2026.s: Mental health disorders are one of the biggest public health and economic challenges in Finland. At some point in life, one in two Finns experiences a mental disorder, but only about half of those with a condition receive the treatment they need. The cost of mental health disorders alone to Finland is over EUR 11 billion per year. Access to treatment is slow in many places, and ho
fi-la-36-2026.t: Act amending section 53 (a) of the Health Act, sections 25a and 45 of the Social Welfare Act and section 10a of the Law on Higher Education

fi-la-37-2026.f: Legislative initiative amending section 5 of the Act on social and health care charges
fi-la-37-2026.s: On 21 September 2026, the Board of Directors submitted to the Parliament of Finland a proposal HE 185/2026 vp setting a new operating fee for health care from 1 March 2027. The fee would be up to EUR 264,10, or 10% higher than the current daily surgery fee (EUR 233,80). The tax procedure for soft drinks is laid down in the Tax Act (182/2010, Valmvol) and the Act on the Tax Procedure for Self-Initiative Taxes (768/2016, OVML).

fi-toim-vero-376606.s: This guide deals with the taxation of pension income in situations where a person lives in Finland and receives a pension abroad, or a person resides abroad and receives a pension from Finland. A reference to the definition of income from Finland for family pensions (Chapter 4.2.4) and the elimination of double taxation when the United States taxes a US citizen resident in Finland on grounds of nationality, although the tax agreement would not otherwise give the United States the right to tax (Chapter 5...).
fi-toim-vero-376606.t: Taxation of pension income in international situations

fi-toim-vero-379577.s: This guide deals with the household allowance granted on the basis of the cost of maintenance and basic improvement of the dwelling, which has been updated retrospectively as a result of changes in Articles 127a, b and f of the Income Tax Act (1535/1992, TVL) which entered into force on 1 January 2026. The maximum amount and the compensation rates for the household allowance have been increased as from 1 January 2026:
fi-toim-vero-379577.t: Household allowance for works resulting from maintenance and basic improvement of dwelling and from abandonment of oil heating

fi-toim-vero-379578.s: This guide deals with the household allowance on the basis of the costs of normal domestic, care and nursing work, which has been updated retroactively as a result of changes in Articles 127a, b and f of the Income Tax Act (1535/1992, TVL) which entered into force on 1 January 2026. The maximum amount of the household allowance and the reimbursement rates have been increased as from 1 January 2026 as follows:
fi-toim-vero-379578.t: Household allowance for normal domestic, nursing and nursing work and for physical and functional therapy

fi-toim-vero-379684.s: This guide deals with the general conditions of the household allowance, which apply regardless of the nature of the work entitled to the allowance. Works entitled to and not entitled to the household allowance are listed in the table.

fi-toim-vero-379810.s: This Guideline deals with the obligations described in the Law on the disclosure of reporting financial institutions in the field of taxation, including the information that reporting financial institutions shall collect and report to the tax administration by means of an annual notification and the due diligence procedures by which reporting financial institutions shall verify the accuracy of the reported information.
fi-toim-vero-379810.t: Tax Administration Guidelines on Reporting Requirements for Reporting Financial Institutions (CRS / DAC2)

fi-toim-vero-380530.s: The guide deals with VAT on the sale of scrap and scrap of metal, which has been subject to the reverse charge since 1 January 2015. The purpose of the introduction of the reverse charge is to reduce the loss of value added tax resulting from fraudulent activities and to improve the competitive situation of honest enterprises in the sector. The reverse charge is intended, inter alia, to prevent a procedure whereby the buyer deducts VAT which the seller fails to pay to the State.
fi-toim-vero-380530.t: Reverse VAT obligation on the sale of scrap and scrap metal

fi-toim-vero-380939.s: The data on the regular taxation of income tax to be transmitted to natural persons and entities and collective benefits for the tax year 2025 shall be made public on 12 November 2026. Data on the change tax to the tax year 2025 shall not be made public until 20 November 2026.
fi-toim-vero-380939.t: Public data on income tax, tax year 2025

fi-toim-vero-380964.s: This guidance deals with the tax treatment of capital loans and losses of other credit claims granted by a natural person and a estate to a limited liability company and a cooperative, in particular the nature of the subordinated debt and other credit claims as an asset under the Income Tax Act and the tax treatment of their transfer and loss situations in the light of the case-law of the Supreme Administrative Court.
fi-toim-vero-380964.t: Disposal and loss of capital loans and other loans granted to the company in the form of income tax

fi-toim-vero-382836.s: This guide deals with the taxation of temporary agency workers from abroad to Finland or to Finnish vessels for water or air, as well as with the procedural instructions for temporary workers, foreign temporary agency employers and the employer of work in Finland. Information has been added that from 2027 the new tax agreement between Finland and France allows the taxation of temporary work in the country of employment from the first day of employment.
fi-toim-vero-382836.t: Foreign temporary agency workers and Finland's taxation

fi-tpa-100-2026.f: Initiative to launch national data centre strategy and overall impact assessment of data centre projects
fi-tpa-100-2026.s: The rapid increase in investment in the data centre challenges the capacity of the electricity system, the adequacy of energy generation, the investment needs of electricity networks and the ability of municipalities to assess the overall impact of projects, while ensuring national security of supply, overall security and the interests of taxpayers.
fi-tpa-100-2026.t: on the launch of the national data centre strategy and the overall impact assessment of data centre projects

fi-tpa-77-2026.f: Initiative for measures on the re-use of discarded batteries for repair
fi-tpa-77-2026.s: On 3 July, guidance published by the Finnish Agency for Authorisation and Control (LVV) on the handling and waste testing of spent batteries threatens to make the repair of electric and hybrid cars virtually impossible for independent car repair companies, and threatens to end the repair of batteries in Finland altogether.
fi-tpa-77-2026.t: Reuse of discarded batteries for repair

fi-tpa-78-2026.f: Initiative to ban the production, import and sale of halal- meat in Finland
fi-tpa-78-2026.s: The starting point of Finnish animal welfare legislation is that, in the case of slaughter, the animal is stunned before the bloodshed, so that it does not cause unnecessary pain and suffering, but this main rule has been exempted on religious grounds.
fi-tpa-78-2026.t: prohibiting the production, import and sale of halal meat in Finland

fi-tpa-79-2026.f: Initiative for measures to break down the deteriorating literacy process
fi-tpa-79-2026.s: The PISA results from 2025 describe the reduced skills of Finnish young people in literacy, mathematics and natural sciences. It is particularly worrying that the decline in literacy has continued throughout the 2000s. Finland is well known for a long time for its most equal school system in the world and for its excellent PISA results.
fi-tpa-79-2026.t: Measures to break down declining literacy trends

fi-tpa-80-2026.f: Initiative to reduce fuel prices by reducing the distribution obligation
fi-tpa-80-2026.s: Due to the significant increase in fuel prices, a reduction in the obligation to distribute fuels towards the EU minimum level is being undertaken.
fi-tpa-80-2026.t: Reducing fuel prices by reducing the obligation to distribute

fi-tpa-81-2026.f: Initiative for measures to protect minors against sexual events that are not appropriate for age
fi-tpa-81-2026.s: According to the Youth Act, ensuring the conditions for youth work is one of the tasks of the municipalities. Municipalities can organise their activities in the way they wish and using the partners. In some cases, this has led to activities that jeopardise children's and young people's right to safe development and to work at the age level. For example, the City of Helsinki organised the sewing work of the Packer and Packer bags on 25 June 2026.
fi-tpa-81-2026.t: on the protection of minors from sexual events that are not appropriate for age

fi-tpa-82-2026.f: Initiative to strengthen wild boar hunting to prevent the spread of African swine fever
fi-tpa-82-2026.s: African swine fever (ASF) is a serious threat to the Finnish pig economy, agriculture and forestry, domestic food production and security of supply. To prevent the spread of the disease, effective and proactive measures are needed, especially to reduce wild boar stock.
fi-tpa-82-2026.t: on stepping up the hunting of wild boar in order to prevent the spread of African swine fever

fi-tpa-83-2026.f: Initiative on intervention by the Russian Shadow fleet through a common European early warning system
fi-tpa-83-2026.s: The Russian Shadow Fleet constitutes one of the most acute security policy and environmental threats in the Baltic Sea. Russia is unscrupulously circumventing the sanctions imposed on the country's energy coasts, thus helping Russia to maintain its war economy, but also helping Russia to maintain the growth of the Shadow Fleet, the use of old and often unfit tanker equipment, and the unclear ownership and insurance regime.
fi-tpa-83-2026.t: on the intervention of the Russian Shadow fleet by a common European early warning system

fi-tpa-84-2026.f: Initiative to correct the calculation of the duration of the student credit without undermining the student's ability to obtain credit for the student's student's student's loan
fi-tpa-84-2026.s: In Finland, a defect has been identified in the regulation of student credit. In the current situation, a student who has performed military or civil service may lose the possibility of student credit for reasons beyond his control.
fi-tpa-84-2026.t: The Court of First Instance held that, in order to determine whether the amount of aid granted by the Member States to the applicant is compatible with the common market, it is necessary to examine whether the aid is compatible with the common market.

fi-tpa-85-2026.f: Initiative for voluntary conversion of development aid
fi-tpa-85-2026.s: Finland's public finances are in a serious situation, the debt of the central government is rising and public expenditure needs to be adjusted, and there are reasons for a critical assessment of secondary public expenditure.

fi-tpa-86-2026.f: Initiative to extend the employment benefit
fi-tpa-86-2026.s: Employee benefits, such as knowledge of lunch, culture and well-being, are an established part of Finnish working life, designed to support the well-being of employees, their working life, access to services, and the ability of employers to take care of their staff. In practice, benefits are offered through a wide range of service platforms such as Edenred, Smartum and Epassi.

fi-tpa-87-2026.f: Initiative to reduce electricity transmission charges
fi-tpa-87-2026.s: As the consumer cannot compete for the electricity transmission of the electricity network company in his region, the price of the network service does not result in normal market competition, which is why the affordability of electricity transmission pricing and effective regulatory oversight are of particular importance.
fi-tpa-87-2026.t: on the reduction of electricity transmission charges

fi-tpa-88-2026.f: Initiative on the impact of co-operation in the chain on competition
fi-tpa-88-2026.s: The Food Market Act was reformed during this government period, and it is now important to monitor that the law also works properly.
fi-tpa-88-2026.t: The effects of chain cooperation on competition

fi-tpa-89-2026.f: Initiative to launch a national quality register pilot for memory disorders
fi-tpa-89-2026.s: Mental diseases are one of Finland's most important growing public health and economic challenges. Finland has nearly 150 000 people with memory problems, and new diagnoses are made every year about 20 000, some of them working age. As the population ages, the number of people with illnesses continues to grow, which increases the need to develop prevention, diagnostics, treatment, rehabilitation and rehabilitation.
fi-tpa-89-2026.t: on the launch of a national register pilot for memory disorders

fi-tpa-90-2026.f: Initiative to provide for a mandatory disciplinary penalty for an ex-post session
fi-tpa-90-2026.s: According to the Basic Education Act, a student who interferes with the teaching or otherwise violates the order of the school or acts in a fraudulent manner may be ordered to sit for up to two hours.
fi-tpa-90-2026.t: on the introduction of a mandatory disciplinary penalty for the ex-post session

fi-tpa-91-2026.f: Initiative on speeding up the flow of information by public authorities on security-relevant authorisation issues
fi-tpa-91-2026.s: There have been serious shortcomings in the flow of information between authorities in situations where a person's right to conduct a profession subject to authorisation is affected by a conviction for a criminal offence.
fi-tpa-91-2026.t: on speeding up the flow of information by public authorities on security-relevant authorisation issues

fi-tpa-92-2026.f: Initiative to reduce the number of prison sentences and increase the maximum penalty
fi-tpa-92-2026.s: The Finnish penal system provides a discount for the perpetrators of more crimes. When multiple offences are dealt with at the same time, the penalty does not accumulate fully. This is called a large-scale discount.
fi-tpa-92-2026.t: on reducing the number of prison sentences and increasing the maximum penalty

fi-tpa-93-2026.f: Initiative to tighten the eligibility criteria of the Minister so that the Minister can only have Finnish citizenship
fi-tpa-93-2026.s: section 60 (1) of the Constitution states that the Council of State shall comprise a Prime Minister and a sufficient number of other ministers who must be Finnish citizens who are known to be honest and competent. The qualification of the Minister is therefore Finnish citizenship. However, the current regulation does not prevent a person acting as a minister from having, in addition to Finnish citizenship, one or more other States:
fi-tpa-93-2026.t: Strengthening the eligibility criteria of a minister so that the Minister can only have Finnish citizenship

fi-tpa-94-2026.f: Initiative to strengthen the employment of people with disabilities and persons with partial employment through a binding model
fi-tpa-94-2026.s: The employment gap between disabled and non-disabled persons is about 20.5 percentage points, which shows that current measures are not sufficient to ensure equal access to the labour market.
fi-tpa-94-2026.t: establishing the employment of disabled people and persons with partial employment through a binding model

fi-tpa-95-2026.f: Initiative on the return of the small group system corresponding to observation categories to basic education
fi-tpa-95-2026.s: The peaceful working conditions in schools, the safe learning environment for pupils and the right of every child to receive education in accordance with their individual needs require that, in basic education, adequate resources are available to meet the different learning, behaviour and school needs.
fi-tpa-95-2026.t: on the return of the small group system corresponding to the observation categories to basic education

fi-tpa-96-2026.f: Initiative for measures to safeguard alternative ways of dealing and to deliver service mail to people over 75, including by letter to prevent digitisation
fi-tpa-96-2026.s: Digital government and the digital skills needed in everyday life cause great difficulties for many older people. According to the old Commissioner, there are up to 500,000 to 600,000 people living in Finland who have no basic digital skills or lack the skills to do independent digital business.
fi-tpa-96-2026.t: on the protection of alternative forms of access and the delivery of service mail to persons over 75 years including by letter to prevent digitisation

fi-tpa-97-2026.f: Initiative on the introduction of pneumococcal vaccine in the national vaccination programme
fi-tpa-97-2026.s: The aim of the national vaccination programme is to protect Finns as well as possible against preventable diseases at the right time and at the lowest possible doses of vaccine. Vaccines included in the national vaccination programme are voluntary and free of charge. They are given at the clinic, school health care or at their own health centre.
fi-tpa-97-2026.t: on the administration of pneumococcal vaccine to a national vaccination programme

fi-tpa-98-2026.f: Initiative to limit the total amount of fees for non-parliamentary trust missions
fi-tpa-98-2026.s: At the same time, decisions can be taken at several levels of government in the context of trust measures in the municipality, welfare area or province. Therefore, the decision-making body can be at its best at four different levels of government.
fi-tpa-98-2026.t: on the limitation of the total amount of fees for trust missions other than those relating to parliamentary representation

fi-tpa-99-2026.f: Initiative to increase the penalties for rape offences, always condemning rape to unconditional imprisonment
fi-tpa-99-2026.s: The current legislation on minimum penalties for rape offences is far too lax: according to Section 1 of Chapter 20 of the Penal Code, rape is punishable by imprisonment for at least one and up to six years, and a maximum of two years' imprisonment can be imposed subject to general provisions. In practice, basic forms of rape can be sentenced to conditional imprisonment below two years.
fi-tpa-99-2026.t: on the punishment of rape offences, always condemning rape to unconditional imprisonment
